info.title: Portcullis — Redis Bridge
info.description: Shields the UI from direct Redis access. Exposes a full Redis operations API (key browser, server info, pub/sub, MONITOR stream, keyspace analysis, slow log, memory stats, and more). Includes a single-call `/overview` endpoint for monitoring dashboards and queue-depth monitoring for List and Stream keys.

get.description: SCAN the keyspace. Pass the returned `cursor` back in the next call until cursor is 0 (scan complete). Use `type` to filter by data type (requires Redis 6.0+). Each result includes key name, type, and TTL.
Auto-detects type and returns value. Large strings are truncated at 1 MB. Collections support `offset` + `count` pagination.

put.description: Replaces the key entirely. Supports string, hash, list, set, zset.

get.summary: Queue depth overview — all List and Stream keys, sorted by depth
get.description:
Scans up to `max_keys` keys matching `pattern` and filters to those of type `list` or `stream`. Returns depth (LLEN / XLEN) and, for streams, consumer-group count and total pending messages. Results sorted descending by depth so the busiest queues appear first.

Uses SCAN + pipeline TYPE check (not SCAN TYPE filter) so it is compatible with Redis 6.0 and PaaS-managed instances.

get.summary: Queue detail — depth, sample messages, and consumer-group status
get.description:
**List keys**: returns `length` and up to `sample_count` entries from the head of the list (LRANGE 0 sample_count-1).

**Stream keys**: returns `length`, `XINFO GROUPS` (name, pending, last-delivered-id, lag — null on Redis < 7.0), per-group pending count via XPENDING summary form, and the age (seconds) of the oldest unacknowledged message derived from the stream entry ID timestamp.

post.summary: 🔒 Move every matching List entry to the top or bottom of the queue
post.description:
Moves all entries of List `key` matching `term` to the **top** (head, index 0) or **bottom** (tail), keeping relative order inside both groups. `term` is a case-insensitive substring, or a whole-value glob if it contains `*` or `?`.

To avoid reordering a moving target, the list is renamed to an unused temp key, reordered there, and renamed back. The reordered content stays first; entries pushed to `key` during the move are appended after it atomically — nothing is overwritten. Consumers see an empty queue for the duration of the move.

get.summary: Environment snapshot — Redis stats and top queues in one call
get.description:
Returns a high-level snapshot of the Redis instance without requiring multiple round-trips from the UI.

**Redis section** includes: connected clients, used memory, keyspace key count, ops/sec, hit rate, and top queue depths (up to `queue_max_keys` scanned).

If Redis is unavailable the section contains `{"status": "error", "detail": "..."}`. HTTP status is always **200**.
